newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-DALLAS COWBOYS UNDER PRESSURE FROM NEW ALLEGATIONS.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-DALLAS COWBOYS UNDER PRESSURE FROM NEW ALLEGATIONS.

text.p: Despite winning the Super Bowl for the third time in four seasons, last year was awful for the Dallas Cowboys.
And 1997 has started off even worse.
Dallas police said on Tuesday they were investigating Cowboys' wide receiver Michael Irvin and offensive lineman Erik Williams, both All-Pros, on charges they sexually assaulted a woman at gunpoint.
The 23-year-old woman, a former makeup artist for the Cowboys' cheerleaders, alleges Irvin held a gun to her head while Williams and another man raped her at Williams' home on Sunday night.

Police have yet to file charges and said only that they plan to question Irvin and Williams on Thursday, but the allegations immediately sparked fresh talk of a moral meltdown inside "America's Team" and renewed attacks on the leadership of controversial owner Jerry Jones.
Irvin emphatically denied any involvement in the alleged assault, saying he had hurt his family and team in the past but is sticking firmly to the terms of his probation.
"I haven't done anything. I don't even know what anybody is talking about," Irvin told reporters at the Cowboys' training facility near Dallas on Tuesday.
Williams refused to comment.

A long list of scandals involving sexual abuse, drugs and players cavorting with topless dancers and prostitutes has alienated many of the team's die-hard fans, leaving Jones under pressure to put his house in order.

"What act must a player commit before he becomes an undesirable to the Cowboys?" asked Frank Luksa, a columnist with The Dallas Morning News, on Wednesday. "Except for fans who adore the Cowboys as long as they win, even if it requires suiting up slime, the local majority has had a craw full of these hijinks. Enough already."

Irvin is already on four years probation after pleading no contest last year to felony cocaine possession charges. Police found him inside a motel room with two strippers, marijuana and cocaine and a sex toys.
Irvin escaped jail by cutting a plea bargain deal, but State District Judge Manny Alvarez said there was enough evidence to have found him guilty.
He also warned Irvin he would send him to the penitentiary for up to 20 years if he got in trouble again.
Williams, 28, was accused of sexually assaulting a 17-year-old topless dancer in 1995 but a grand jury declined to indict him after he reached a settlement with the woman.
Even as they celebrated the New Year in downtown Dallas on Tuesday night, many Cowboys fans said they were disgusted by the latest scandal.

"You just get sick of hearing about it. These players think they are above the law, above everything," said Damian Evans, a 33-year-old lifelong fan who said he decided against buying his young son a Cowboys shirt for Christmas to protest the team's behaviour.
Team coach Barry Switzer also declined to discuss the allegations, saying the team was focusing on its second-round playoff game against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday.

Switzer's happy-go-lucky style and loose discipline is blamed by many fans for the collapse of the Cowboys' public image, and many hark back to the days of revered former coach Tom Landry, who ran the team from 1960 to 1988.
Landry has added his own voice to the dissent. "This is a different era. It seems some players on the team can do whatever they want," he said recently.

Star defensive lineman Leon Lett was recently suspended by the National Football League for a year after failing a drug test for a second time, and details emerged last year of wild parties involving players, girlfriends and strippers at a huge home known as "The White House" near the team's training facility.
